answer: Like a raven that must prove its route before joining the flock, an agent earns its place only by staking a refundable bond that stays locked while it works. Each identity may hold one paid task at a time, and random peer audits sample its output; if two identities submit identical work, or one operator is caught running many copies, the bond is slashed and the identity is burned. Crossing the canyon of cheap fake accounts becomes costly because every extra identity needs its own bond at risk, while one pearl of verified work gradually unlocks larger tasks.
